purpose: Authoritative-provider review adding ERPNext + Frappe HR as a metadata-driven manufacturing ERP/HCM/payroll source at spec-verified. Current provider documentation confirms tenant-instance HTTPS REST APIs, token/API-key authentication bound to a Frappe user and its roles, Frappe v15+ API v2 DocType metadata, list pagination/filtering, configurable rate limiting, and optional HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks. No credentials, customer data, production mutation, payroll mutation, on-prem network access or write-back were used.

systems.name: ERPNext + Frappe HR
systems.evidenceNote: Provider-owned Frappe documentation confirms generated REST APIs for DocTypes, token authentication using API key+secret, user-role permission enforcement, v1 and v15+ v2 APIs, v2 DocType metadata reads, list pagination and filtering, configurable fixed-window rate limits, and optional HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks. ERPNext/Frappe HR documentation establishes Work Orders, Job Cards with employee/time logs, Workstations, downtime, inventory/Stock Entry, Employee Checkin, shifts/attendance, timesheet-linked salary slips and other ERP/HR objects. Exact installed apps, custom DocTypes, field permissions, site URLs and regional customisations are tenant-specific and require authorised proof.
securityEvidenceBlockers: Frappe API tokens inherit the selected user's roles and permissions rather than carrying an independently narrow API scope. Before authentication evidence advances, prove a dedicated non-admin integration user whose effective DocType/document/field access is limited to the required read set and whose write paths are denied.

The REST/RPC surface can execute whitelisted methods and CRUD mutations. WFM must use a reviewed GET/read route allowlist; arbitrary /api/method calls, POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE and document methods such as submit/cancel/rename remain disabled.

Frappe data masking is permission-aware on ordinary ORM/API responses, but provider documentation warns that custom SQL/Query Reports can bypass automatic masking. Custom reports/methods are not trusted read surfaces until separately reviewed.

requiredPermissions: use a dedicated Frappe integration user rather than Administrator or a human account
grant read permissions only to required DocTypes and documents/entities; prove field-level masking and company/site restrictions in the authorised tenant

pin the customer-approved HTTPS instance host; never follow arbitrary/cross-host redirects and place private/on-prem instances behind the customer edge/gateway rather than cloud-scanning plant networks
prefer token/OAuth authentication over password/session authentication for unattended runtime
allow only reviewed GET/read endpoints such as /api/resource or /api/v2/document and, where available/authorised, /api/v2/doctype/{doctype}/meta
keep RPC/whitelisted methods, file uploads and all write verbs disabled unless a later use case receives separate write-roundtrip approval
if webhooks are used, require Webhook Secret/HMAC verification plus replay/idempotency controls and scheduled read reconciliation
prove API key/secret rotation and revocation and keep credential material out of catalogue/evidence/log payloads
dataAvailableOrExpected: Company, Employee and organisation references where Frappe HR is installed/configured
Shift Type, Shift Assignment, Attendance and Employee Checkin with IN/OUT timestamps and optional biometric device/location context
Leave/absence and other HR DocTypes where the installed Frappe HR version and permissions expose them
Work Order, Operation, Workstation and Job Card production context; Job Cards include assigned employee, time logs and completed quantity
Item/BOM/product, Warehouse, Stock Entry, WIP/material-transfer and serial/batch inventory context
Downtime Entry and related workstation/machine operational evidence where used
Timesheet, payroll/Salary Slip and finance dimensions where Frappe HR/ERPNext modules are installed and explicitly authorised
Purchase/supplier/procurement and sales/order/project references where explicitly mapped
custom fields and custom DocTypes created by the customer or regional/local apps; these must remain source-attributed extensions until mapped
stableIdentifiers: Frappe DocTypes use the document 'name' as the primary key; preserve DocType + name + instance/site identity as the external key
child-table row names and parent links must be preserved for nested/time-log/material records rather than flattening by display label
customer-created naming series, UUIDs or custom identifiers must not be assumed globally unique across companies or separate ERPNext instances

freshnessLatency.rest: polling freshness is determined by connector cadence and tenant response time; use modified timestamps/filters plus overlapping windows rather than assuming realtime completeness
freshnessLatency.webhooks: can reduce latency when configured with a Webhook Secret, but remain event signals rather than completeness proof and require scheduled reconciliation
freshnessLatency.onPrem: private/self-hosted instances may be intermittently reachable; preserve source modified/effective time separately from ingestion/recovery time

paginationDeltaEvents.pagination: v1 resource lists support limit_start and limit_page_length/limit; v2 list operations also support pagination. Use bounded deterministic pages and stable ordering where the tenant/version allows it.
paginationDeltaEvents.delta: use filters on the standard modified timestamp with an overlap window and primary-key dedupe; do not claim a change-token/CDC contract unless a specific tenant/version proves one
paginationDeltaEvents.metadata: Frappe v15+ exposes GET /api/v2/doctype/{doctype}/meta, enabling metadata-driven field/custom-field discovery when the integration user is authorised
paginationDeltaEvents.webhooks: Frappe can emit DocType webhooks and optionally signs payloads with X-Frappe-Webhook-Signature using HMAC-SHA256; unsigned hooks are not acceptable WFM business-data authority

rateLimitsAndRetries: Frappe rate limiting is site-configurable and based on request execution time in a fixed window, so no universal numeric limit should be hard-coded
HTTP 429 must throttle/back off and retain page/checkpoint state; retry only idempotent reads automatically
401/403 on static token credentials stops blind authentication retry and enters credential/permission diagnostics
use bounded exponential backoff with jitter for retryable network/5xx failures and replay the last overlap window after recovery
large backfills must checkpoint by object/company/time window and reconcile expected/received counts where count endpoints or tenant reports are available
versionsRegionsCustomFields: Frappe API v1 is broadly available; API v2 and DocType metadata endpoints are documented for Frappe v15+, so connector discovery must negotiate the installed major version rather than assuming v2
ERPNext/Frappe can be Frappe Cloud or self-hosted on a customer-specific domain; private/on-prem hosts require customer-edge placement or an approved gateway
installed apps differ by tenant; Frappe HR/payroll objects must be feature-discovered rather than assumed present on every ERPNext site
DocTypes are metadata-driven and customers can add Custom Fields/property setters or entire custom DocTypes; fingerprint metadata and preserve unmapped fields as extensions
preserve company/entity, country, currency, site timezone, locale, units/UOM and local payroll/tax identifiers without globally flattening them
multi-company and acquired-business deployments may use separate ERPNext sites with colliding document names; instance/site identity is part of the canonical external key
automationOpportunities: use one ERPNext/Frappe connection to bootstrap people, shifts, attendance, production, inventory and finance mappings for small manufacturers instead of separate implementation projects
compare Work Order/Job Card demand and completed quantity with scheduled qualified labour to forecast overtime/agency pressure and redeploy internal capacity
join Job Card employee/time logs to payable WFM labour cost for labour-per-order/operation/unit attribution without treating Job Card time as payroll truth
join material availability/WIP and Work Order demand to avoid assigning scarce labour to jobs blocked by missing materials and to redirect capacity to executable work
use downtime/workstation evidence with skills/availability to coordinate maintenance labour and reduce paid idle time
reconcile Employee Checkin/Attendance against WFM expected shifts and payroll evidence to identify missed punches, off-shift work and payroll-risk exceptions
use metadata discovery to propose customer-specific mappings for custom fields while requiring review for semantic/type-breaking drift
preserve company/cost-centre/project/warehouse dimensions so executive reporting can attribute labour and production outcomes across sites/entities
savingsHypotheses: micro and mid-market manufacturers already using ERPNext can reduce integration implementation effort by using one metadata-driven source for workforce, production, inventory and finance context rather than commissioning multiple point integrations
reduce overtime/agency spend by combining work-order/job-card backlog with actual scheduled labour and internal availability before shortages become end-of-shift emergencies
reduce paid idle time by detecting jobs that are labour-ready but material-blocked, or material-ready but skill-constrained, and reallocating workers earlier
improve payroll accuracy by reconciling Employee Checkin/Attendance with WFM shift and payroll evidence while keeping payroll authority separate
improve order/product costing by joining Job Card execution and output with authoritative labour cost, inventory and finance dimensions
reduce manual mapping maintenance by detecting additive custom fields automatically and escalating only breaking schema drift
causalOutcomeReadiness: preserve ERPNext instance/site + DocType + document name, source modified time and ingestion time for every operational record
preserve recommendation/action IDs and baseline/outcome windows when workforce changes are made against Work Order/Job Card/downtime signals
retain competing changes such as material receipt, machine recovery, priority/order change and maintenance action so labour decisions are not falsely credited for correlated throughput movement
dataGaps: no authorised tenant was available to prove exact installed ERPNext/Frappe/Frappe HR versions, app set, role permissions, custom DocTypes/fields, instance topology or real object schemas
provider docs define generic REST capabilities but customer-specific permissions determine which records/fields are actually readable
Frappe rate limits are tenant-configurable, so numeric quotas and practical throughput must be measured per site
Frappe HR/payroll is not guaranteed to be installed/configured on every ERPNext instance
Job Card/Checkin operational time is not authoritative payable time unless the customer explicitly designates and validates it
no production-quality event model should be inferred unless the tenant has the relevant Quality DocTypes/data and mappings enabled
constraintsRisks: API tokens inherit user roles and can become over-privileged if generated for Administrator/System Manager or a broad human user
generic Frappe REST includes write CRUD and whitelisted RPC methods, so route/method allowlisting is mandatory
custom SQL Query Reports/custom methods can bypass automatic field masking; do not use them as ordinary connector shortcuts
self-hosted versions and custom apps can diverge materially from cloud/current documentation
document names can collide across separate sites/companies and must be namespaced by instance/site
unsigned Frappe webhooks are spoofable; only secret-signed events behind replay/idempotency controls can be trusted
metadata/custom-field growth can silently change customer mappings unless schema fingerprints and review-required drift rules are enforced
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Obtain an authorised ERPNext/Frappe test site spanning one current v15+ instance and, if commercially justified, one older/self-hosted version. Create a dedicated non-admin integration user and prove exact host/site identity, read-only role effects, denied write/RPC paths, token rotation/revocation, v1/v2 version negotiation, v2 DocType metadata/custom-field discovery, modified-time pagination/backfill, signed webhook verification, multi-company identity, timezone/currency/UOM semantics and recovery from 429/network outage/duplicate webhook/schema drift. Keep payroll/production mutations disabled.
